chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a house that fell upon a group of people who were gathered together, so it was not known which one of them died first. He said: 'They inherit from each other.'

I said, 'But Abu Hanifa has included something in it.' He said, 'And what has he included?' I said, 'Two men, brothers, one of them was my slave and the other was a slave of another man. For one of them was a hundred thousand dirhams, and the other had nothing. They both sailed in the ship, so they drowned, and it was not known which of the two died first. The wealth is for the inheritors of the one who had nothing, and nothing will be for the inheritors of the one who had the wealth.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He (Abu Hanifa) has heard it, and it is like this.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when multiple people die simultaneously and the order of death is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of mutual inheritance among simultaneous deceased parties, a ruling confirmed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) as being consistent with the view of Abu Hanifa. The narration highlights the practical application of this rule in cases of uncertainty, such as drowning or collapse, where the chronological order of death cannot be determined. It serves as a key reference in Shia jurisprudence for resolving inheritance disputes in mass casualty events.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a house which fell upon a people who had gathered (and they all died).
So it was not known which one of them died first’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would inherit from each other’.

I said, ‘But Abu Haneefa has included something in it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what has he included?’ I said, ‘Two men, brother, one of them was my slave and the other was a slave of another man. For one of them was a hundred thousand Dirham, and the other one, there was nothing for him. They both sailed in the ship, so they drowned. So it was not know which of the two died first. The wealth is for the inheritors of the one who had nothing for him, and nothing will be for the inheritors of the one who had the wealth’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He (Abu Haneefa) has heard it (the answer), and it is like this’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has narrated the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about a people on whom a house falls and they all die. It is not known who has died first. He (the Imam) said, ‘They all inherit each other.’

I then said, ‘Abu Hanifah has introduced something in it.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What has he introduced?’ I said, ‘Two men who were brothers, one of them was my Mawla’ (slave) and the other was a Mawla’ of another man. One of them had one hundred thousand dirham and the other did not have anything. They embarked on a ship but they drowned and it is not known which one died first, the legacy belongs to the heirs of the one who had nothing and the heirs of the one who had the asset does not receive anything.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘He (abu Hanifah) has heard it (the answer) and that is the way it is.’”
